clue.text: Lazy, like a creature with three toes

definitions.meaning: idle and slow to make any effort

definitions.text: like a creature with three toes
definitions.meaning: resembling the three-toed sloth, the slow-moving tree-dwelling mammal

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: sluggish and idle, and read literally as resembling the three-toed tree mammal.

clue.text: Her cue to develop the game in America

indicators.note: letters that develop change into something new, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snooker player gives her the cue so she can develop her game in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Euchre is a trick-taking card game long popular in the United States.

clue.text: Jailhouse adieus expressed in musical narratives

parts.note: the can is slang for a prison
ta-tas are informal British goodbyes

explanation.surface: Prisoners' farewells set to music as sung stories.
explanation.walkthrough: TA-TA is an informal British way of saying goodbye; 'expressed in' simply links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantatas are vocal works, often telling a story in several movements for voices and instruments.

clue.text: and 21,8 5 6 20's battered tea urn, devil to turn, no extra tea

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of shape, so the long run of words is rearranged

parts.words: tea urn, devil to turn, no extra tea
parts.note: the letters rearranged, which hold the full line with its 'next'
the cross-reference to 21 across, whose letters are part of the line but not of these lights

explanation.surface: A tea urn has taken a beating and the devil has run off with the last of the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give the whole line including NEXT; 21 across holds NEXT, so the lights 4, 19 and 8 take the rest. 'and' is the word printed between in the enumeration.
explanation.definitionFit: The line is the opening of Walter Savage Landor's short poem 'Dying Speech of an Old Philosopher'.

clue.text: Aquatic creature Washington gets almost churlish about

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

indicators.note: turned about means the word is written backwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: surly means churlish and rude

explanation.surface: A sea animal is treated a bit rudely by someone from Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: WA is the US postal code for Washington state; 'almost' trims the churlish word before 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The walrus is a large tusked marine mammal of Arctic waters.

clue.text: It's wet around lake, wild country, nothing right for a poet

indicators.note: the wet word goes around the letter for lake

parts.note: water is the thing that is wet
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
a land is a country
O is the shape of zero, nothing
savage means wild or untamed

explanation.surface: A wet, wild landscape seems fit for a Romantic poet to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: The lights run 5, 20, 6, so the grid holds the surname before the middle name; 'for' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Savage Landor was an English poet and writer of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: See 5 down
Nearly see Tzar replaced as substitute

indicators.note: letters replaced are put back in another order
nearly all of the word, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone almost sees a Tsar swapped for a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts SEE to SE; 'replaced' rearranges SE and TZAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means a substitute, usually an inferior imitation of the real thing.

clue.text: See 4
Grab the eggs!

definitions.meaning: to seize hold of something tightly
a set of eggs laid at one time by a bird

explanation.definitionFit: A clutch is both a tight grip and a nestful of eggs laid together.

clue.text: Explosion disrupted t' bus tour

indicators.note: disrupted letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire-accented complaint about trouble on the bus tour.
explanation.definitionFit: An outburst is a sudden explosion of feeling or activity.

clue.text: Will's ego?

parts.note: read as the part that goes with 'will' to make a word for stubbornness, and also one's ego

explanation.definitionFit: Self-will is stubbornness, and a person's ego is their own identity.

clue.text: Woman at court, people with backstreet laws

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name
men are people
a back street: ST, the abbreviation for street, read backwards

explanation.surface: A woman at court with some men from a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backstreet' is one printed word read as 'back street', ST turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Enactments are laws or statutes passed by a legislature.

clue.text: John being introduced to the two couples is yummy!

indicators.note: one piece is put into the middle of another

parts.note: a foursome is two couples together
john is slang for a toilet, as is lav

explanation.surface: John being brought along to meet two couples is a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: John is not a man here but American slang for a toilet, as lav is in Britain; 'being introduced to' puts it inside the couples' word.
explanation.definitionFit: Flavoursome means full of flavour, tasty.

clue.text: Violent opening, taking in eastern border

indicators.note: the opening word takes in, or contains, the other pieces

parts.note: a vent is an opening
a hem is a border on cloth

explanation.surface: A violent breach that swallows an eastern frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful, passionate, violent in feeling.

clue.text: He knows how to act, notedly fading away

parts.note: a man is a he
can means knows how to
do means act

explanation.surface: An actor can, by his skill, fade away gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notedly' points to musical notation: this is a score marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Mancando is an Italian musical direction meaning dying away in volume.

clue.text: Tart, say, raised from the edge

parts.note: a flan is an open tart

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A tart, perhaps, lifted off from the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A flange is a projecting rim or edge on an object.

clue.text: Former class player said to go too far

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: said signals a word spoken that is spelt differently

parts.note: a seed is a ranked player in a class of competitors

explanation.surface: A former classmate is said to have gone too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' means CEED is spelt to sound like SEED, a ranked tournament player.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed is to go beyond a limit.

clue.text: Hunt the poet for Beatles' first sellout; it makes a cheerful jingle

annotationWithheld.why: Hunt the poet for Beatles' first sellout; it makes a cheerful jingle: LEIGH + B go inside SELL, but the one printed word 'sellout' is both the SELL piece and its container indicator 'out'
annotationWithheld.clue: Hunt the poet for Beatles' first sellout; it makes a cheerful jingle

clue.text: See 4
See 5 down
Certain extras to be included will follow

indicators.note: the word is included within the run of clue letters

explanation.surface: Certain extras will be added later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be included' signals letters inside 'certain extras'.
explanation.definitionFit: What is next comes after and so will follow.

clue.text: Trendy ex is one who'll spill the beans

parts.note: in means trendy, fashionable
ex means former

explanation.surface: A fashionable ex is one who'll talk to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer gives secret information, idiomatically spilling the beans.

clue.text: Tidy number initially being taken in

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is used

parts.note: eaten means taken in as food

explanation.surface: Tidy up the number first before it is taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: making something neat and orderly is tidying it.

clue.text: They all leave the river to topless relative

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Everyone departs from the river to see a topless relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes the A off AUNT. EXEUNT is the Latin stage direction for actors leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the stage direction meaning they leave the stage, all going off.

clue.text: Doubled over and collapsed

definitions.meaning: having failed or gone under, as a business does

explanation.definitionFit: Folded means creased double, and also describes a business that has closed down.
